cohort: 439 women in the third trimester of pregnancy (34.1 ± 3.7 weeks)
finding: Both insomnia alone and comorbid insomnia/habitual snoring were associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including excessive daytime sleepiness, gestational hypertension, and large for gestational age infants.
mod_finding: Women with habitual snoring alone were at increased odds of having an unplanned cesarean section.
